newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Dec housing completions rose 3.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Dec housing completions rose 3.2 pct.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department report on completions of new privately-owned housing units, seasonally adjusted annual rates, in 1,000s, with percent changes from prior months and year over year.
Housing completions by region, seasonally adj., in 1,000s:
For all of 1996, unadjusted actual completions rose 7.4 percent to 1.410 million units from 1.313 million in 1995.

The department said completions of single-family homes rose 1.1 percent in December after a revised 1.4 percent rise in November and a revised 0.2 percent increase in October. Previously, the department said single-family completions rose 0.4 percent in November and fell 0.1 percent in October.

December multi-family unit completions rose 11.4 percent after a revised 13.3 percent rise in November and a revised 4.2 percent decrease in October. Previously, the department said November multi-family unit completions rose 9.8 percent and that October multi-family unit completions were off 5.4 percent.

The department said actual completions on an unadjusted basis rose in December to 139,900 units from 121,600 units in November and from 129,900 units in October. In December 1995, actual completions were reported at 115,300.

Privately-owned housing units under construction fell to a seasonally adjusted 820,000 in December from 828,000 in November and from 823,000 in October. They compare with 800,000 units under construction in December 1995.
